permissions.title: Permissions & devices
permissions.why: Summo needs the microphone to record. The audio never leaves this machine — the permission belongs to your operating system, not to us.
permissions.fix_browser_chrome: Click the lock (or slider) icon at the left of the address bar → Site settings → Microphone → Allow.
permissions.fix_browser_firefox: Click the crossed-out microphone in the address bar and unblock, or Settings → Privacy & Security → Permissions → Microphone.
permissions.fix_browser_safari: Safari → Settings → Websites → Microphone → set this site to Allow.
permissions.fix_macos: macOS grants microphone access to the **application**, and here that application is {app}: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone → enable {app}. If you started Summo from a terminal, enable it for the terminal.
permissions.fix_windows: Settings → Privacy & security → Microphone → turn on “Let apps access your microphone” and “Let desktop apps access your microphone”.
permissions.fix_linux: Check the input is not muted in PulseAudio/PipeWire (`pavucontrol` → Recording), and if the browser runs in Flatpak, grant it `--device=all`.
permissions.fix_retry: Come back here and press “Check again”. Summo does not need restarting.
permissions.system_linux: Supported: Summo uses the default output's monitor source through PulseAudio/PipeWire. Nothing to install.
permissions.system_windows: Supported: Summo uses WASAPI loopback. Nothing to install.
permissions.system_macos: macOS has no built-in route for this. The only way is a virtual device (BlackHole, Loopback) selected as an input — Summo does not ask for the Screen Recording permission to do it, because an audio recorder should not demand the right to watch your screen.
permissions.system_unknown: Whether this machine can capture system audio has not been determined.
permissions.fix_macos_any: macOS grants microphone access to the **application**, and here that is the browser you have Summo open in: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone → enable it. If you started Summo from a terminal, enable it for the terminal.
permissions.notify_why: Reminders when a draft is waiting or a task is overdue. Nothing is sent anywhere; the notification is drawn by this machine.
permissions.notify_browser_chrome: Click the lock icon at the left of the address bar → Site settings → Notifications → Allow.
permissions.notify_browser_firefox: Settings → Privacy & Security → Permissions → Notifications → unblock this site.
permissions.notify_browser_safari: Safari → Settings → Websites → Notifications → set this site to Allow.
permissions.notify_macos: macOS: System Settings → Notifications → {app} → turn on “Allow notifications”. Then check Focus (Do Not Disturb) is off — with Focus on, the permission still reads granted and you see nothing.
permissions.notify_macos_any: macOS: System Settings → Notifications → the browser you have Summo open in → turn on “Allow notifications”. Then check Focus (Do Not Disturb) is off.
permissions.notify_windows: Windows: Settings → System → Notifications → enable it for the browser, and turn off Focus assist / Do not disturb.
permissions.notify_linux: Linux: check your desktop's Do Not Disturb setting, and note that a Flatpak browser needs access to the D-Bus notification service.
permissions.notify_unsupported: This browser has no notification API — Summo will remind you inside the app instead.

help.title: Help 🛟
help.lead: The questions people actually ask, each with the button that acts on it.
help.privacy_a: No. Speech recognition and speaker separation run on models on your machine — pull the network cable and recording still works. Two things need the network: summarising and asking questions, because they call a language model, and you choose that endpoint in Settings (it can be Ollama on this same machine). Translation runs on a model inside the app.
help.record_q: Do I need a bot in the meeting?
help.record_a: No. Summo captures the microphone and the system audio on your own machine, so it works with Zoom, Meet, Teams, a phone call, or people in a room — anything your computer can hear. Press record, talk, press stop.
help.models_q: What is a model, and which do I need?
help.models_a: The model is the part that listens and writes words. Start with the one the Models screen recommends: it measures your machine and says which will keep up with live audio. Install a larger one later if you want a more accurate pass after the meeting.
help.files_a: In ~/.summo/vault, as ordinary Markdown. Open it in Obsidian, grep it, put it in git, back it up. Summo reads those same files back, so editing them elsewhere is fine. Recordings live in ~/.summo/audio and you set how long they are kept.
help.assistant_q: What does the assistant answer from?
help.assistant_a: Only what is in your vault. Every answer carries a citation pointing at the meeting and the timestamp it came from; click it and you land there to check. If the vault does not contain the answer, it says so.
help.translate_q: Can it translate, and does that need the network?
help.translate_a: Yes, 46 languages, on a model inside the app — no Ollama, no network. Translate as you record from Settings; translate a recording you already have from the “Export & translate” card on the meeting.
help.shortcuts_a: Press ? anywhere for the full list. The two worth remembering: ⌘K (Ctrl+K) searches and jumps to anything, and ⌘⇧R starts and stops recording even when the window is hidden.
help.stuck_q: Recording will not start, or something failed
help.stuck_a: Three places, in order: Settings › Recording for the microphone permission and the device; Models to check a speech model is installed; Settings › Intelligence and “Test connection” if the failure was about summarising or asking. If it still will not go, report it with the sentence the app showed you.
